We instead formulate part decomposition as a joint partitioning of the entire shape, where the predicted parts are non-overlapping and jointly recover the entire shape. author: Hao-Tang Tsui, Yu-Rou Tuan, Xiaoxuan Ma et al.

summary: Robots deployed in the physical world must be able to improve beyond their initial training as they encounter new situations and failures. A growing body of work attempts to close this gap by injecting 3D awareness into MLLMs, either by boosting fine-grained pixel-level cross-view correspondence or by fusing features from 3D geometry foundation models, yet a substantial gap to human reasoning persists. summary: The dynamics of generative models exhibit two apparently distinct temporal windows: a speciation window, in which a sample commits to a semantic class, and a nonlocality window, in which local context windows become insufficient for generation. author: Zihan Wang, Zhen Wu, Pieter Abbeel et al.

author: Yi Pan, Haocheng Xi, Kan Zhu et al.

author: Joseph Metcalfe, Sara Sharifzadeh, Fabio Caraffini

summary: Answering questions about long videos often requires connecting events involving the same objects across hours or days. summary: A small trainable advisor can steer a frozen language-model executor using natural-language advice. summary: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE), popularized by large language models, is a promising paradigm for scaling visual generative models. summary: Language-model (LM) harnesses enable LMs to operate effectively over long contexts using additional compute. author: Teng Zhou, Yunhao Chen
